question: How a ship walks its path plan, and what advances plan+34h.
answer: plan+34h is a step cursor into the path, not a node count. Nine writers exist in the image; eight store zero and the only advance is ADD dword [ESI+34h],1 at 009E421F inside 009E3C00, taken when the ship is inside the look-ahead of its target node or has been carried past it AND 00417EF0 reports the straight run from the ship to the node after the target clear of avoid zones.

runtime_evidence.what_it_establishes: The executable still records 009E3C00, so this run did not reach the reconstructed body and cannot confirm the projection. It does establish the input: 009EC680 is also a record, so all six seeded plans stay in state 1 with a two-node ship-to-goal graph, and the follower would run the two-node path on all 468 picks.
runtime_evidence.static_prediction: Wiring the follower leaves path_publishes at 0 on this mission, because a two-node plan sets record+20h = 1 and never reaches 009E4243, so 009EE5F9 keeps taking the skip. What changes is blk+A94h/+A9Ch, which would stop taking the pose and start taking the goal, and 009D9E50's answer at 009EE6AC. Unverified: src/game_hosts_ship_ai.cpp belongs to packet cc_exe_2q.

uncertainty: 00417EF0's true-means-blocked polarity rests on 00417E90 having the same body shape and the same two callees; 004179D0 itself was not read.

The x87 intermediates that are multiplied or divided and only then stored are modelled in double and rounded once. The exact-product cases (the overshoot test at 009E40DD) are reproduced exactly; the divide cases (009E3EB3, 009E3EC6, 004F3A78, 004F3AA8) can differ by one ulp from an 80-bit divide rounded to float32.
0082E850's return reaches 009E3EB3 as an 80-bit value; the reconstruction takes it as a float before scaling.
The reconstruction is build-tested only. No native differential fixture exists for 009E3C00, and no run reaches it (see runtime_evidence).
